newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares continue correction, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares continue correction, end lower.

text.p: Greek equities traded in negative territory continuing Monday's strong round of profit taking to end with light losses in moderate turnover. Brokers expected the correction to bottom out around 920 points.
Floor traders said news of the U.S. missile attack on Iran had a minor impact with light concern centered on rising oil prices.

"The market was not affected by the attack on Iraq. Stocks are balancing out, the current phase is described by profit taking of short term gains with buying interest intact as buyers are lurking at slightly lower levels," said Nick Creticos, floor trader at Midas Securities.

The bourse's construction sector was still attracting interest and the market would bottom out at around 920 points, most likely to be reached intraday on Wednesday, before another climb unfolds, he said.

The Athens general share index closed 0.33 percent, or 3.07 points lower at 930.84 from Monday's 933.91 close after opening at 933.27 points. Turnover rose to 7.04 billion drachmas from 5.69 billion on Monday on volume of 4.3 million shares.
Bankers and economists forecast August inflation would ease to 8.5 percent year-on-year from 8.6 percent in July, they told Reuters in an informal poll.
Greece will hold early elections September 22.

Other brokers said the correction was nearing its end around 930 points and the market's uptend remained intact. Players got jittery on Monday on talk that the gap between the competing socialist Pasok and conservative New Democracy parties seemed to be closing.
